title: U.S. House · California's 44th District
area: South Bay and harbor-area Los Angeles County, including San Pedro, Wilmington, Carson and parts of Long Beach, redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Nanette Barragán (D) and Republican Genevieve Angel advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating a Democratic write-in candidate.

candidates.name: Nanette Barragán
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Nanette Barragán is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in California's 44th District. A Harbor Gateway native and attorney, she served on the Hermosa Beach City Council before her election to Congress in 2016, when she became the first Latina to represent the district. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and has chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

background.text: According to her official biography, she was born and raised in the Harbor Gateway area of Los Angeles, the youngest of eleven children of immigrant parents from Mexico. Wikipedia gives her birth date as September 15, 1976 and says she attended North Torrance High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2000 and a law degree from the University of Southern California in 2005.
Early in her career she worked in the Clinton White House Office of Public Liaison and with the NAACP Washington Bureau, according to Wikipedia.

Worked as an attorney at Latham & Watkins LLP, handling matters from land use to securities litigation, and took leave in 2012 to work on the Obama re-election campaign's voter protection team in Florida, per Wikipedia.

Elected to the Hermosa Beach City Council in 2013 (serving 2013-2015), the first woman elected to the council in ten years, according to her official biography; she led the opposition to a proposal to drill 34 oil and water injection wells in Hermosa Beach.
Her official biography says her council peers chose her as mayor, the city's first Latina mayor; Ballotpedia describes the role as mayor pro tempore.
Elected to the U.S. House in November 2016 as the first Latina to represent California's 44th District, and was chosen freshman class president and a regional whip in the 115th Congress.

Serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee (subcommittees including Health, Energy and Communications and Technology) and is a Co-Chair of the House Democratic Steering and Policy Committee, according to her official biography. She became the first Latina in 10 years on Energy and Commerce in 2019.
Became chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus in January 2023, according to Wikipedia; she is also a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

priorities.text: Says she has consistently fought on behalf of the Affordable Care Act and will fight to preserve and strengthen health care reforms that make quality, affordable coverage accessible to all.

Says her district endures disproportionate environmental injustices and that the country should focus on transitioning to a clean energy economy by electrifying transportation and expanding renewables.
Says she is dedicated to ensuring access to affordable housing and supports combining housing market-driven solutions with federal, state and local initiatives.

positions.summary: Supports legislation to end the ban on gun violence research at the CDC, close background-check loopholes, and ban devices that convert semi-automatic rifles into machine guns.
positions.quote: I support legislation to eliminate the prohibition on gun violence research at the Centers for Disease Control. It's unconscionable that the agency has been effectively barred by Congress from researching injuries and deaths related to firearms. I also support closing loopholes in the national firearm background check system, and banning devices that turn a semi-automatic rifle into a machine gun, like we saw in the horrific shooting in Las Vegas.

positions.summary: Says she has consistently fought on behalf of the Affordable Care Act, which expanded Medicaid coverage in California, and will fight to preserve and strengthen it.
positions.quote: Healthcare is a fundamental right. Throughout my time in Congress, I have consistently fought on behalf of the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Says the country should focus on transitioning to a clean energy economy by electrifying the transportation system and increasing use of renewables rather than relying on fossil fuel infrastructure.
positions.quote: Instead of risking the public health of the frontline communities across the country, we should be focused on transitioning to a clean energy economy by electrifying our transportation system and ramping up our use of renewables.

positions.summary: Says she will continue to advocate a pro-labor agenda that includes raising the minimum wage to $15.00 per hour.
positions.quote: I will continue to advocate for a pro-labor agenda, including raising the minimum wage to $15.00 per hour and ensuring Davis-Bacon Act protections remain in place.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology, Health, and Environment subcommittees) for the 2025-2026 term.
Chaired the House Homeland Security Committee's Border Security, Facilitation, and Operations Subcommittee during the 2021-2022 term.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026-specific campaign website statements or Candidate Connection survey responses were found. Positions above are drawn from her official House issues pages, which otherwise consist of press-release listings without further statements matching the fixed issue set (e.g. no direct statement on abortion, immigration enforcement, or housing zoning/supply was found).

candidates.name: Genevieve Angel
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Genevieve Angel is the Republican candidate in California's 44th District and is running for office for the first time. She describes herself as a Filipina-Latin American mother, wife, small-business owner, family nurse practitioner and healthcare executive. In her Ballotpedia survey she lists economic affordability, public safety, healthcare reform and immigration reform among her priorities.

background.text: Describes herself as an immigrant and as Filipina-Latin American; her survey says she graduated from St. Theresa's College high school (1988 in an earlier survey submission).

Earned a nursing degree from the University of Santo Tomas in 1992, an MBA from American International University (Los Angeles) in 2007, and a nursing master's degree from United States University in 2025, according to her survey (Ballotpedia's infobox lists the latter two as graduate degrees).
Career as a registered nurse, family nurse practitioner, small-business owner and healthcare executive; she says she has served families in the 44th District "for nearly three decades."

A BallotReady profile lists past roles including chief executive of Huntington Park Community Care (2008-2013), chief nursing officer of Olympia Medical Center (2015-2016) and chief nursing officer at UHS (2023-2024).
Is a first-time candidate who describes herself as "not a politician"; she advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary and reports endorsements from Reform California and the LA GOP.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on fiscal responsibility, public safety, healthcare reform and educational freedom.
priorities.quote: I bring a unique, hands-on perspective to the table. With a background as a Family Nurse Practitioner and healthcare executive, I'm committed to strengthening our community through fiscal responsibility, public safety, healthcare reform, and educational freedom.

priorities.text: Economic affordability, public safety, healthcare reform and immigration reform (her listed policy areas).

candidates.researchNotes: Only Ballotpedia survey responses found; no campaign website located. Responses give topic lists without specific positions.
